My preference is y > x > w > z. My priority at each school is: w: 1, x: 2, y: 1, z: 2. Most applicants favor y > x > w > z.

I want to maximize my chances of getting my most preferred school, y. Since I have the highest priority (1) at y, and most applicants also favor y, I should propose to y first.

If I get rejected from y (unlikely given my top priority), I will propose to my second choice, x. My priority at x is 2. Since most applicants favor x after y, there's a chance I will be rejected from x.

If I get rejected from x, I will propose to my third choice, w. My priority at w is 1. Since w is less preferred than x and y by most applicants, I have a good chance of being accepted at w.

Therefore, my ranking should be: y > x > w > z. This strategy ensures I aim for my most preferred school with high priority, and if rejected, I proceed to my next best option. If rejected again, I have a high chance of securing my third choice due to my high priority there and the overall preferences of other applicants.
reasoning.Student B:
My preference is z > y > x > w. My priorities are: w: 2, x: 1, y: 2, z: 1. Most applicants favor y > x > w > z.

I should start by proposing to my most preferred school, z. I have priority 1 at z, so I have a good chance of getting in.

If I get rejected from z, I'll propose to my second choice, y. I have priority 2 at y. Since most applicants favor y > x > w > z, y is likely to be competitive. I might get rejected.

If I get rejected from y, I'll propose to my third choice, x. I have priority 1 at x. Since most applicants favor y > x > w > z, x is less competitive than y, but more competitive than w and z. Given my high priority, I have a good chance of getting in.

If I get rejected from x, I'll propose to my last choice, w. I have priority 2 at w. Since most applicants favor y > x > w > z, w is likely the least competitive. I might get in, but it's my least preferred option.

Considering these scenarios, the best strategy is to stick to my preferences. Proposing to z first gives me the best chance of getting my top choice, given my priority 1. If rejected, proposing to y is still better than going to x, although the chance of rejection is higher. If rejected from y, I can fall back on x, where I have priority 1. Finally, w is my last resort.

Therefore, the ranking should be z > y > x > w.
